title: Asymptotically uniform expected maximum bucket for linear hashing
summary: Prove that random linear hashing has expected normalized maximum bucket size tending to one below source min-entropy by a linear gap.

formal_statement.body: Fix a prime power $q$ and $\epsilon>0$. Let $Z$ be an arbitrary distribution on $\mathbb F_q^n$, choose $m\le H_\infty(Z)-n\epsilon$, and let $H$ be a parity-check matrix of a uniformly random $[n,n-m]_q$ linear code $C$. Prove that $\mathbb E_C[\lVert q^m P_{HZ}\rVert_\infty]=1+o_n(1)$ uniformly over all admissible source sequences, or exhibit a source family that refutes this limit.

scope.domain: Expected maximum-bucket uniformity of random linear syndrome hashing
assumptions: The source is an arbitrary q-ary distribution with prescribed min-entropy
The hash is the parity-check map of a uniformly random fixed-dimension linear code
The output length satisfies a fixed positive linear gap below source min-entropy
scope.unresolved_remainder: For binary sources, Dhar--Dvir concentration combined with the later Jaber--Kumar--Zuckerman quadratic tail bound yields the normalized expected limit $1+o_n(1)$, first for flat sources and then for arbitrary sources by the source's flat-source decomposition. Proving or refuting the same limit for every fixed field size $q>2$ remains open.

progress.summary: Dhar and Dvir prove that, in the dense binary flat-source regime, every bucket has relative load $1+o(1)$ with high probability; by itself this does not control rare large buckets in expectation.

progress.summary: The later quadratic max-load tail bound makes the normalized binary loads uniformly integrable. Combined with Dhar--Dvir concentration, full-rank conditioning, and flat-source decomposition, it closes the binary branch in expectation; fixed fields $q>2$ remain unresolved.
